confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from three web searches. Aggregators such as citycost.org, nomad.watch and jobicy showed a budget meal at about A$18-28, a cappuccino at about A$4.50-5.50, a 0.5 L local beer at about A$7.40 and a mid-range dinner for two at about A$73-115. Some of these figures come from crowdsourced or modelled data, have mixed dates, and look low for Byron Bay's tourist pricing in 2026. I moved them upward using judgement, and the mid-range meal for two is set to reflect a full three-course meal. Searching for cocktail and wine prices found only happy-hour specials, such as A$6-7 schooners, A$6-8 house wine and A$12-14 cocktails, and no regular menu prices. So the cocktail and wine anchors are estimated from their usual relationship to the beer price above happy-hour levels, and they are less certain. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge only, with no booking pages or listings checked. They assume July 2026, which is winter low-to-shoulder season, but Byron Bay accommodation is structurally expensive and swings widely with events and weekends. Treat them as low-to-medium confidence.
comparable_city_reasoning: Byron Bay is a premium coastal resort town in northern New South Wales. Restaurant and bar prices are roughly at or above Brisbane, Gold Coast and inner-Sydney casual dining levels. Accommodation costs are well above typical regional Australian towns and close to premium Australian beach destinations such as Noosa.
